paper_metadata.title: Research on microstructure and properties of Ti-15Mo-3Al alloy with high oxygen content

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: In this paper, the near-equilibrium microstructure and properties of Ti-15Mo-3Al-1O alloy treated by solid solution at different temperatures were systematically studied.

evidence.section: 2. Materials and methods
evidence.quote: Ti-15Mo-3Al-1O alloy was prepared using pure titanium rod(99.9 mass%), granular pure aluminum(99.99 mass%) and molybdenum powder and TiO2 powder by non-consuming vacuum arc melting in a water-cooled copper crucible using a tungsten electrode under argon atmosphere.

evidence.section: 2. Materials and methods
evidence.quote: Ti-15Mo-3Al-1O alloy was prepared using pure titanium rod(99.9 mass%), granular pure aluminum(99.99 mass%) and molybdenum powder and TiO2 powder by non-consuming vacuum arc melting in a water-cooled copper crucible using a tungsten electrode under argon atmosphere. All the ingots were turned over and melted at least three times repeatedly to ensure homogeneous composition.

evidence.section: 1. Introduction
evidence.quote: the samples from Ti-15Mo-3Al-1O ingots treated with solution at 800 ∼ 1, 200 °C for 2 ∼ 8 h, followed by water quenching (hereinafter referred to as solution treatment)

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: the alloy subjected to solution treatment at 1,100°C/2 h and 1,200 °C/2 h exhibited excellent compressive ductility(The specimens were not crushed, the strain δ>50%) with high compressive yield strength(YS>1,100Mpa).

evidence.section: 3.1 As-cast microstructures of the Ti-15Mo-3Al-1O alloy
evidence.quote: there were a large number of α phase (the black area) precipitated in coarse original β grains. Although the alloy was solidified in a water-cooled copper crucible with a great cooling rate, there were still a large number of α phases precipitated in grains because of the addition of 1wt.% oxygen content. According to the SEM micrograph, α phase in grain precipitated in the form of fine needles

evidence.section: 3.1 As-cast microstructures of the Ti-15Mo-3Al-1O alloy
evidence.quote: The results showed that there were only α and β phases in the as-cast alloy. As can be seen from the relative intensity of diffraction peaks, there was mainly α phase in the as-cast alloy.

attributes.size: length about 2–5 μm, width about 0.1–0.2 μm
attributes.morphology: stripe-like intragranular, grain boundary and intergranular

evidence.section: 3.2 Microstructures of the Ti-15Mo-3Al-1O alloy after solution treatment at different temperature
evidence.quote: The length of the intragranular α phase was about 2–5μm and the width was about 0.1–0.2μm. The intragranular α phase was stripe-like

evidence.section: 3.2 Microstructures of the Ti-15Mo-3Al-1O alloy after solution treatment at different temperature
evidence.quote: there was only β phase without α phase or oxide when the alloy was subject to solution treatment at 1,100°C for 4 h and 1,200 °C for 2 h respectively.

evidence.section: 3.2 Microstructures of the Ti-15Mo-3Al-1O alloy after solution treatment at different temperature
evidence.quote: there was only β phase without α phase or oxide when the alloy was subject to solution treatment at 1,100°C for 4 h and 1,200 °C for 2 h respectively.

evidence.section: 4.1 Effect of 1% O on the microstructure of the alloy subjected to solution treatment at different temperature
evidence.quote: when temperature was lower than 900 °C, Ti6O phase would precipitate in titanium alloys containing more than 2.8 wt% oxygen element

evidence.section: 4.2 Effect of 1% O on deformation behavior of Ti-15Mo-3Al alloy at room temperature
evidence.quote: there were a large number of evenly and finely dispersed α phases in the microstructure of the alloy subjected to solution treatment at 800°C and 900°C, which played an important role of precipitated-phase strengthening.

evidence.section: 4.2 Effect of 1% O on deformation behavior of Ti-15Mo-3Al alloy at room temperature
evidence.quote: oxygen was dissolved into α and β phase to improve solution strengthening effect.

evidence.section: 4.2 Effect of 1% O on deformation behavior of Ti-15Mo-3Al alloy at room temperature
evidence.quote: the generation of twins and martensite also improved the ductility of the alloy due to TRIP and TWIP effects during deformation of β-type titanium alloy
